Imagine if the image hosting boards didn't have dedicated image hosting. That would be a major constraint on the usability of the site if users had to look around the web for an image host.

For the security conscientious, the fewer sites you have to use to post something artistic, funny, satirical, or insightful the less likely you are to get doxxed or have your computer compromised by malicious script.

Adding temporary image hosting doesn't have to be a major drain on memory or slow the performance of the site significantly if the size of the images uploaded is limited. Because image size can be adjusted, Voat can determine how much more in bandwidth costs it's willing to accept. If Voat has accurate and stable statistics on its bandwidth usage and can accurately estimate the excess bandwidth used monthly for image hosting, image size can be altered each month to keep it below what Voat is already paying for most of the time while not interfering with usability.

The limited time before image files are deleted will reduce the risk of getting hasslesome DMCA notices and take down requests since the images will be deleted before most copyright lawyers even realize it's there and possibly before most of the images ever show up in google image search.
